name: United States, California Vehicle Code 21800-21804 (right-hand traffic), as applied to WOMD maps
status: validated by review: rules checked on CAT's 500 WOMD scenes by reading the trajectories and figures of every flagged crossing (see references/validation-us-california.md); the person's own labels were not used as ground truth. Citations checked against the text of the Vehicle Code on 2026-10-30.
notes: 21800(a): a driver approaching an intersection yields to a vehicle that has already entered it from a different highway. At an all-way stop the engine uses arrival at the stop line as the observable stand-in for entry: both stop, and the first to stop is normally the first to enter.
21800(c): at an all-way stop, two vehicles entering at the same time (here: arriving within 1 s): the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

21800(e)(3) and 21801(a): when vehicles approach from opposite directions and one turns left or makes a U-turn, 21800 does not apply; the turner yields to oncoming vehicles close enough to be a hazard. This rule is applied before yield_right.
When both were already waiting when the clip began the order is unknown and no verdict is given: the one that goes first while the other waits is ordinary turn-taking, not evidence of a violation.
21802(a), (c): at a stop sign the driver stops and yields to vehicles approaching from another highway; this does not apply where every approach has a stop sign (the all-way rules above).

21800(b)(1), (b)(2): on a simultaneous entry the driver on a terminating highway (a T junction) yields to vehicles on the continuing highway. The profile applies it whenever the junction has no sign, before the other rules.

Uncontrolled junctions apply only the left-turn rule. The statute's first-entered (21800(a)) and yield-right (21800(b)(1)) rules were tried and held for no more than chance on the 500 scenes, because the map usually lacks the signs or lights that really control such a junction. us-california-statute applies them as written.

21804: a vehicle entering from a private road or driveway yields to traffic on the highway. Signalised pairs (21451, 21453, 21801 on green) are decided by the CAT right-of-way code, not by this profile (no green_rules).
A complete stop is required by law but is not used to label aggression: the clip starts mid-approach, so a stop before step 0 cannot be seen.

21453(a)-(c): on a circular red, stop; then a right turn (or a left turn from a one-way street onto a one-way street, which the map cannot tell) is allowed, yielding to pedestrians and to vehicles close enough to be a hazard. A red arrow forbids its movement. red_turn encodes this; the screen reports it in sdc_red_entry / ooi_red_entry.

CVC 21950(a): yield to a pedestrian crossing within a marked crosswalk, or an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection (crosswalk 'on', unmarked_crosswalk_at_intersection). 21950(b): a pedestrian may not suddenly leave the curb into the path of a vehicle too close to stop (the screen's stepped_out_late). 21950(c), (d): due care toward any pedestrian in a crosswalk.
CVC 21954(a), (b): elsewhere on the roadway the pedestrian yields to vehicles close enough to be an immediate hazard, and the driver keeps due care (unsignalised_road 'care').

CVC 21451(a): on a circular green, a driver, including one turning, yields to pedestrians lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk; on a green arrow (21451(b)) crossing pedestrians face a red, so only due care. 21453(b): a turn on red yields to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk.
CVC 21952: before driving over or upon a sidewalk (a driveway), yield to any pedestrian approaching on it (sidewalk_crossing).

Turning across a cyclist going straight (a right hook, or a left turn across an oncoming cyclist): a cyclist has the rights of a driver (CVC 21200), so 21451(a) and 21801(a) give it priority over the turner.

CVC 21760(c) (Three Feet for Safety Act): do not overtake a bicycle closer than 3 ft (0.91 m) between any part of the vehicle and any part of the bicycle or its rider; change lanes first where another lane is available (not checked); 21760(d): where 3 ft is impossible, pass slowly and only when it does not endanger the cyclist. No statutory distance for pedestrians (null: the screen's physical fallback).
